A Father's Struggle To Stop His Daughter's Adoption

In addition to the expected blood-boiling aspect of this case, it gets me thinking about registries in general, and how to make laws that can adapt to the reality that nearly half the children born in America today are illegitimate.

This particular case was very cut-and-dried - the biological father could prove that the biological mother had willfully deceived him, and he used the putative father registry to establish his right to be notified of and to contest the adoption. For him, the legal mechanisms the state put in place to give unmarried putative fathers legal standing actually worked.

Which is just peachy, as he wanted to raise the child... but these same laws that gave him much-wanted rights give a lot of other unmarried men much-unwanted responsibilities. I'm of the opinion that biological parenthood must either confer rights AND responsibilities, or no rights and no responsibilities. The fact that a baby has half of your DNA either establishes a legally significant tie between you or it does not - in other words, we can't create a situation where unmarried biological fathers can't be assessed child support, but CAN block adoptions or sue for custody. So who gets shafted here - the highly sympathetic men who want to raise their children conceived out of wedlock, or the less-sympathetic but far larger population of men who want nothing more than to avoid being saddled with "accidental" children? If forced to pick one group to help, I'd pick the guys paying child support on children they never wanted to be born - that would do the greatest good for the greatest number, and would serve as a social corrective to women who conceive accidentally-on-purpose without the consent of their partner. But what of the guy who wants the "oops!" baby? Other than registries (which everybody seems to agree don't work), how is he to differentiate himself from the single father who doesn't want to be legally tied to the child? Is the solution to make a national registry and promote the hell out of it?

If I post non-goat material (or anti-goat material) then I am less likely to gain influence.
